sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Nebraska, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Friday, October 23Passed

Your application must reach your county election office by 6 p.m. on Friday, October 23, 2026 (the second Friday before the election) for a ballot to be mailed to you. After that you can still vote early in person at the county office until Monday, November 2. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be received by the time polls close on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026: 8 p.m. Central time (7 p.m. Mountain time). A postmark is not enough; it must arrive by then. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Monday, November 2, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Nebraska’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Nebraska or in another state? What Nebraska says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Any registered voter can ask for an early voting ballot by mail. You do not have to give a reason. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Print the state's early voting ballot application, fill it in, sign it by hand, and mail it to your county election office. You can also write a letter with the same details (your name, home address, Nebraska driver's license or state ID number, phone, the address to mail the ballot to, and your signature). Open it (official page)
  • Email or fax. Sign the paper application by hand, then take a picture or scan of it and email it, or fax it, to your county election office. Typed or electronic signatures are not accepted. The state's pages offer no online request form. Open it (official page)
  • In person. You can vote early in person at your county election office (see early voting below). Someone you choose (an agent) can also request and pick up a ballot for you; one agent can do this for no more than two voters per election. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it back in the return envelope. Leave time for it to arrive by 8 p.m. Central (7 p.m. Mountain) on Election Day. (official page)
  • Drop box. Put it in your county's secure drop box. The state lists drop boxes on its Drop Box Locator page. (official page)
  • In person. Bring it to your county election office yourself, or have someone you choose (an agent) deliver it. (official page)

What the envelope needs

You must sign the application by hand and give ID: write your Nebraska driver's license or state ID number on it, or send a copy of another accepted photo ID (a Nebraska college ID with your name and photo counts), or a Reasonable Impediment form if you cannot get an ID. An ID number given over the phone is not accepted. If you asked for your ballot this way, you do not show ID again when you send it back. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Nebraska’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 5, 2026 to Monday, November 2, 2026.

Vote early in person at your county clerk or election commissioner's office from Monday, October 5, 2026 (the first day under the state's 30-days-before rule) through Monday, November 2, 2026, the day before the election. (official page)

Students

At school in Nebraska, away from home

A Nebraska student at a college in another Nebraska county can stay registered in their home county; leaving home for college does not have to change where you live for voting. A student can instead register in the county where they go to school if they mean to make that their home and are usually there. Registering at school does not change your residence for tuition. (official page)

At school in another state, with Nebraska as home

The state's student page does not speak separately to a Nebraska student at school in another state. Its general rule is that leaving home for college does not by itself change where you live for voting. Students from another state who attend school in Nebraska can vote in their home state. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military voters, their families and U.S. citizens living overseas can use the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA), which registers you and asks for a ballot at once; send a new one each calendar year. Your ballot is sent the way you choose on the form; email is preferred, or fax or mail. The Federal Write-in Absentee Ballot is accepted as a backup. Under the federal guide, the request must arrive by 6 p.m. October 23, 2026 and the ballot by 8 p.m. Central (7 p.m. Mountain) November 3, 2026. (federal guide)

Nebraska in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The request deadline is two days away as of October 21, 2026: 6 p.m. Friday, October 23. Your county election office can confirm its hours.
  • The application says: if you are living away from home for a while (at school, for example), give the address where you are registered as where you live, and put your temporary address as where to send the ballot.
  • Voters in a by-mail precinct are sent a ballot automatically. They write their ID number on the return envelope, or enclose a copy of an accepted ID or a Reasonable Impediment form.
  • A copy of your application is a public record before the election (name, home address, precinct, mailing address and dates).

polls:
Polls are open 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Central time, and 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Mountain time, so all close at the same moment. (the law)

  • rest of the state: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. CST
  • The Panhandle and the southwest: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. MST

Anyone in line when the polls close may still vote.
